CWE-20.name: Improper Input Validation
CWE-20.definition: Input is accepted without validating the properties required for safe and correct processing.

CWE-22.name: Path Traversal
CWE-22.definition: External input constructs a pathname that can escape its intended directory.

CWE-59.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access
CWE-59.definition: A file access path can resolve through a link to an unintended resource.

CWE-78.name: OS Command Injection
CWE-78.definition: External input alters the syntax or behavior of an operating-system command.

CWE-79.name: Cross-site Scripting
CWE-79.definition: User-controlled input is placed into web output without adequate neutralization.

CWE-90.name: LDAP Injection
CWE-90.definition: External input changes the structure or meaning of an LDAP query.

CWE-94.name: Code Injection
CWE-94.definition: External input changes the syntax of generated code or executable instructions.

CWE-95.name: Eval Injection
CWE-95.definition: Input is evaluated dynamically without neutralizing language directives.

CWE-114.name: Process Control
CWE-114.definition: Untrusted input controls which process or library is executed.

CWE-120.name: Classic Buffer Overflow
CWE-120.definition: Input is copied into an output buffer without checking that it fits.

CWE-134.name: Externally-Controlled Format String
CWE-134.definition: A format string originates from an external source and controls formatting behavior.

CWE-190.name: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
CWE-190.definition: A calculation wraps around when the logic assumes the result remains valid.

CWE-242.name: Inherently Dangerous Function
CWE-242.definition: A function cannot be guaranteed to operate safely in all uses.

CWE-295.name: Improper Certificate Validation
CWE-295.definition: A certificate is not validated correctly before it is trusted.

CWE-326.name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
CWE-326.definition: Sensitive data uses encryption that is weaker than the required protection level.

CWE-327.name: Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-327.definition: A broken or risky cryptographic algorithm or protocol is used.

CWE-328.name: Use of Weak Hash
CWE-328.definition: A hash algorithm does not provide the expected resistance to recovery or collision.

CWE-330.name: Insufficiently Random Values
CWE-330.definition: Values are predictable where security depends on unpredictability.

CWE-337.name: Predictable PRNG Seed
CWE-337.definition: A pseudo-random generator is initialized from a predictable seed.

CWE-338.name: Cryptographically Weak PRNG
CWE-338.definition: A non-cryptographic pseudo-random generator is used for security-sensitive values.

CWE-377.name: Insecure Temporary File
CWE-377.definition: Temporary files are created or used in a way that exposes data or enables races.

CWE-426.name: Untrusted Search Path
CWE-426.definition: A search path can direct a critical resource lookup to an untrusted location.

CWE-470.name: Externally-Controlled Class or Code Selection
CWE-470.definition: External input selects classes or executable code through reflection.

CWE-502.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
CWE-502.definition: Untrusted data is deserialized without ensuring the resulting object is safe.

CWE-601.name: Open Redirect
CWE-601.definition: A user-controlled destination is used in a redirect without sufficient restriction.

CWE-611.name: XML External Entity Reference
CWE-611.definition: XML entities can resolve to external documents outside the intended control sphere.

CWE-625.name: Permissive Regular Expression
CWE-625.definition: A regular expression accepts a broader set of values than intended.

CWE-643.name: XPath Injection
CWE-643.definition: External input changes the structure or meaning of an XPath expression.

CWE-676.name: Potentially Dangerous Function
CWE-676.definition: A function can introduce a vulnerability when used without its required constraints.

CWE-730.name: Regular Expression Denial of Service
CWE-730.definition: An inefficient regular expression can consume excessive computation on crafted input.

CWE-770.name: Allocation Without Limits or Throttling
CWE-770.definition: Resources are allocated without intended limits on size or quantity.

CWE-785.name: Path Function Without Maximum-sized Buffer
CWE-785.definition: A path operation writes into a buffer smaller than its maximum possible output.

CWE-787.name: Out-of-bounds Write
CWE-787.definition: Data is written past the end or before the beginning of its intended buffer.

CWE-789.name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size
CWE-789.definition: An untrusted size controls allocation without an adequate upper bound.

CWE-829.name: Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
CWE-829.definition: Executable functionality is included from outside the intended control sphere.

CWE-918.name: Server-side Request Forgery
CWE-918.definition: A server fetches an attacker-influenced destination without restricting where it may connect.

CWE-943.name: Special Elements in Data Query Logic
CWE-943.definition: External input changes the intended logic of a data-store query.

CWE-1321.name: Prototype Pollution
CWE-1321.definition: Input modifies object prototype attributes without sufficient control.

CWE-1333.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
CWE-1333.definition: A regular expression has inefficient complexity that can consume excessive CPU.

CWE-1336.name: Template Injection
CWE-1336.definition: External input is interpreted as template syntax by a template engine.
